title: Stage representatives for affine higher-image sections
statement: Let Λ be an arbitrary commutative ring, k:W→S a scheme morphism and G a Λ-module sheaf on W_et [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let I be a small cofiltered category, D:I→Over W an inverse system with affine transitions and qcqs composite structure maps to S, and c a cone whose underlying scheme cone is limiting, with qcqs composite structure map to S. Fix q∈ℤ and an affine etale object V→S. Write G_i=D(i)^*G and G_c=c.pt^*G [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]; write t for the canonical higher-image transition of [def-sbc-module-higher-image-transitions], using higher images as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For every x∈(R^q(c.pt→S)_*G_c)(V), there exist i∈I and y∈(R^q(D(i)→S)_*G_i)(V) with t(c_i)(V)(y)=x. No conclusion about equality or uniqueness of representatives is asserted.

proof.text: Choose a small directed final presentation of I^op. Its opposite is initial, so reindexing preserves the underlying scheme limit. After base change to an affine etale U over S, the stage schemes and limit are qcqs and the transitions affine. The coefficient diagram on the limit is canonically constant with value the pullback of G, by inverse-image composition, and its colimit is that value since I^op is nonempty and connected.

Use an injective module resolution and its underlying abelian-section acyclicity to compute abelian cohomology after forgetting scalars (03FD), without ring flatness. Apply continuity for degree-zero sheaves as complexes (0EZM) to each system of the preceding step. This gives cohomology-presheaf continuity on the affine basis; all maps are the canonical derived-unit maps, hence commute with restrictions and agree with t. The higher-image presheaf description (03Q8) and sheafification of presheaf colimits identify the limit higher image with the sheaf colimit of the stage higher images. For q<0 the resolutions have zero cohomology.

Represent the given limit section locally by stage sections. Refine its cover to a finite affine cover of V with quasi-compact pairwise fibre products. On each overlap, matching in the sheaf colimit is locally witnessed by equality at later stages. Quasi-compactness gives finitely many witnesses per overlap, and there are finitely many overlaps. Filteredness supplies one stage for every representative and matching equality. The stage sheaf condition glues the representatives on V, and their limit image equals the original section on the cover, hence on V. This is the surjectivity argument in 0738(4).
The reindexed stage is already an original stage. Naturality of the presheaf comparison identifies its section map with t(c_i). Thus the representative has the required displayed image.

proof_origin.place: Specialization of 09Z1 and the surjectivity part of 0738 to constant-ring module sheaves; affine section assembly by C3

Second reading with rg on both library roots and the source checkout also found AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.exists_higherDirectImage_affine_section_eq_zero in HigherDirectImageAffineSectionVanishing. It is an abelian-sheaf theorem for a directed preorder, nonnegative degree, and varying coefficients, not the general module-valued canonical-transition statement here. Its use would require reindexing and a natural module/abelian comparison. Abelian stalk analogues likewise do not directly match.
